6\. A refused consult can stop a running pipeline 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability 
Api.consult_refusal calls engine.reload(), which runs the full PlaybookEngine._load(), before
it checks for a busy builder, aux or architect. _load() stops and pauses the pipeline when the
playbook does not load (dirty, uncommitted, wrong config). It also swaps the in-memory playbook and
clears last_rule in the middle of a running job. So a phone consult (asked twice, before and
after the fetch) or a hands consult sent while the builder is working can stop the pipeline. It
can also change which rules decide that builder's end, even though the consult itself is then
refused as busy.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description `Api.consult_refusal` reloads the playbook through `PlaybookEngine._load()` before it checks for busy roles. `_load()` can call `stop()`, which pauses the pipeline and notifies. It also replaces the playbook in force and clears `last_rule` while a job is running. So a consult that is going to be refused anyway can stop a running pipeline or change the rules for the running job. ## Fix Focus Areas - src/hands/api.py[557-591] - src/hands/playbook.py[1623-1627] ## Recommended Fix Run the `_role_busy` checks for architect/builder/aux, and the `kit_wait` check, before calling `engine.reload()`. Only reload once no role is busy. Also make `reload()` side-effect free on failure: load the playbook without `stop()` (for example, a `_load(stop_on_error=False)` variant that only sets `load_error`), so the refusal text reports the load error without stopping the pipeline. Add a test: a consult sent while a builder job is running with a dirty playbook leaves `pipeline.json` unpaused and `last_rule` unchanged. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
